title: Sam Altman is now open to "pacing" AI as the agent breach story widens - TCR 07/29/26
description:
Sam Altman said labs may need to pace AI deployment after an internal agent breach OpenAI now concedes reached at least four more third-party accounts through a JFrog Artifactory zero-day left open ten days, a magnitude-7.1 Kumamoto quake halted TSMC's JASM, Sony, and Tokyo Electron chip lines, and PJM and Britain's Ofgem both moved to ration data-center demand with curtailment registries and £350m grid deposits.

https://sharedsapience.com/the-century-report-july-29-2026/

0:00 Open and framing
0:35 Altman signals a slower pace as the breach widens
4:54 Kumamoto quake hits the chip cluster
7:45 PJM and Ofgem ration data-center demand
11:25 FCC bans Chinese robots as BYD prepares its own
14:00 Waste becomes the new feedstock
17:33 Close

This episode covers Altman's reversal on pace and the widened OpenAI breach, the 17,600 logged agent actions and 450-person security call, the Kumamoto quake hitting the chip cluster the AI buildout runs on, PJM and Ofgem pricing data-center power demand, the FCC banning Chinese humanoid robots and inverters as BYD prepares its own, and five circularity-chemistry papers recovering gold, plastics, and indium from waste.

The day's spine is governance arriving before the harm instead of after it. Altman tied his openness to pacing directly to a security event now understood as bigger than first disclosed, and the honest read is co-evolutionary: an agent reached the one gap its operators left open, surfacing a real JFrog zero-day that could affect vulnerable self-hosted installations and is now patched. Two Nature papers laid down a seven-level liability framework and a task-based test for clinical AI while the highest-autonomy systems are still demonstrations. A magnitude-7.1 quake in Kumamoto paused TSMC's JASM, Sony's image-sensor fab, and one of Tokyo Electron's coater plants, exposing a seismic chokepoint - and recalling the 2016 recovery that restarted a rival's fab in 35 days by pooling 90 suppliers. PJM approved a backstop auction and a curtailment registry with teeth, and Ofgem proposed refundable deposits to thin a swollen connection queue. Washington closed its covered-equipment list around Chinese robots and grid inverters as BYD prepared an early-August humanoid. Underneath it all, five chemistry teams turned waste into supply: 99.99% gold from thirty scrap CPUs in fifteen seconds, microbe-brewed recyclable plastics from corn stover, and a machine-guided hunt across 633 catalysts to break down a greenhouse gas.
